purpose: A Slicer DICOM plugin that detects rotational C-arm XA/XRF multi-frame runs in the DICOM browser. On Load it opens a window to reconstruct them into a 3D volume with FDK and/or SART in PyTorch, and it can subtract a second run (3D DSA).
summary: I read the module, plugin, dialog, DICOM reading, geometry, GE calibration, phantom and display code, plus the CMake files and LICENSE. I did not read reconstruction.py in full. I found no network access, subprocess, eval/exec, pickle or file deletion beyond the extension's own temporary preview folder. PyTorch is handled correctly: it is declared in build_dependencies and EXTENSION_DEPENDS, installed only through PyTorchUtils after a confirmation dialog, and never at import. The license is MIT. CMake installs every imported Python file. Remaining points are non-blocking: the reconstruction runs on the GUI thread with processEvents, no research-use disclaimer, a category mismatch between the catalog and CMake, and a moving `main` revision. 🟢 Recommend merge
